Should Margin Pressure Fears Require Action From Cisco Stock Investors?
sum: Cisco Systems expanded its partner and cloud portfolio, adding Cisco IQ for Partners, new incentives, AI focused tools and quantum resilient networking products to tie more revenue to software, telemetry and lifecycle services around AI era infrastructure.

The same push into AI hardware, cloud control platforms and richer partner incentives brings higher hardware mix and cost pressure that could weigh on gross margins, which has become a key concern in recent research commentary.
We will now look at how Cisco Systems' investment narrative could shift given fresh concern around AI related gross margin pressure.
Scan how Cisco Systems’ AI networking push compares with peers by running the same filter used to surface 52 AI infrastructure stocks that could see momentum as AI buildouts continue.

For Cisco Systems, the core belief is that AI era networking, security and software subscriptions can keep expanding even as hardware intensity puts strain on gross margin. The short term swing factor is how well upcoming earnings and guidance on November 12 line up with expectations for AI driven orders and subscription traction, especially after the recent share price pullback.

The biggest risk right now is that a heavier hardware mix, higher component costs and hyperscaler AI pricing pressure keep eroding margin faster than software, telemetry and services scale. The new partner incentives and AI centric tools are important, but on their own they do not yet change that margin equation in a material way.

The most relevant operational update tied to this debate is Cisco Cloud Control with Cisco IQ for Partners and the broader partner program refresh. These tools give resellers and service providers more telemetry, lifecycle hooks and deal level economics, which relates directly to the push toward recurring software and support tied to AI infrastructure.

Cisco Systems stock downgraded before fiscal first-quarter results
sum: Morgan Stanley downgraded Cisco Systems to Equal-weight from Overweight on Thursday, November 5, and cut its price target to 120 US dollars from 135 US dollars. The move came before Cisco's fiscal first-quarter results, with the bank arguing that the shares now offer a more balanced risk-reward profile.
Cisco Systems stock traded at 86.48 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 13:18 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026.

The downgrade was reported by Investing.com. Analyst Meta Marshall said Cisco's improving demand environment and artificial-intelligence opportunity still support the long-term investment case, but much of the rerating is already reflected in the shares.

Morgan Stanley said Cisco has gained 43 percent over the past 12 months, compared with a 14 percent rise for the S&P 500. The stock has consequently rerated to about 19 times forward earnings, bringing its valuation in line with the broader index.

The bank also pointed to two operating risks. Customers may have brought orders forward ahead of planned price increases, which could flatter near-term sales. At the same time, a larger share of lower-margin hardware sold to hyperscale customers could weigh on gross margins as Cisco expands its AI infrastructure business.

Marshall nevertheless expects Cisco to continue benefiting from earnings growth and sees several years of double-digit growth, particularly through cloud customers. Morgan Stanley said the growth mix will rely increasingly on AI revenue once the company moves beyond the effect of its pricing increases in fiscal 2028.

Cisco is scheduled to report its fiscal first-quarter results after the US market close on Thursday, November 12. Investors will focus on whether demand remains firm after pricing changes and whether the developing AI mix is putting pressure on profitability.

What Could Lift Cisco Stock?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Cisco Systems (CSCO) stock returned 45.9% in the year through November 4, 2026. The S&P 500 returned 14.9% over the same period. Following that run, the shares trade at 30.8 times Cisco’s earnings for the four quarters ending July 25, 2026. That compares with an average P/E of 25.1 across its last twelve fiscal quarter ends. So what in Cisco’s business could lift the shares from here?

All of Cisco’s gain under a three-year scenario would come from selling more. In fiscal 2026, Networking generated most of its extra sales. The Networking business made up 54.7% of revenue that year, with sales rising 22.5%. Services, the next-largest business, remained flat. Cisco is also selling more to AI buyers. On the August 12, 2026 call, management said AI infrastructure for hyperscalers, the largest cloud companies, accounted for about 6% of fiscal 2026 revenue. That figure is up from less than 2% in fiscal 2025.

If Cisco’s revenue grew 10.0% a year for three years, a pace below its fiscal 2026 growth, the shares would be worth about 11.2% more than today. The table below shows Cisco today alongside that scenario.
Cisco would need to sell enough more to offset a slightly lower net margin and a lower P/E. Trefis assumes a lower P/E because the stock currently trades above its own average.

Management guided for fiscal 2027 revenue of $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion. The midpoint of that range sits 15.0% above fiscal 2026. The scenario assumes 10.0% annual growth, trailing the 15.0% guidance, because the scenario is set slightly below Cisco’s fiscal 2026 growth and the guide covers only fiscal 2027.

Cisco posted faster growth in each quarter of fiscal 2026, from 7.5% revenue growth in the first quarter to 17.6% in the fourth, each against the same quarter a year earlier. Management expects AI sales to grow further, projecting $7.5 billion of revenue from AI infrastructure for hyperscalers in fiscal 2027. That compares with about $4 billion in fiscal 2026. Excluding that hyperscale revenue, management said its guidance has the rest of the business growing about 10%.

Cisco (CSCO) Stock Surges 46% in 2026: AI Infrastructure Growth, Earnings, and Outlook
sum: Cisco Systems has outperformed the broader market in 2026, driven by robust demand for AI infrastructure and data center upgrades. Fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $15.84 billion exceeded estimates, with AI-related orders significantly raising management’s annual forecast to $9 billion. While the company is strategically reallocating capital toward AI and security, rising memory costs continue to pressure gross margins. Wall Street remains generally bullish; however, some valuation models suggest limited long-term upside. Current technical indicators show Cisco consolidating within a symmetrical triangle, with investors closely monitoring potential breakouts between $106 and $133.

TradingKey - Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ: CSCO) is one of the most unexpected stocks in the 2026 market. According to Yahoo Finance and Zacks Investment Research, the networking stock is up nearly 46% in value. The rally easily beats both the Nasdaq index performance, as well as the overall 14.6% gains achieved in the Computer and Technology Sector. But for a firm that was once thought of as a legacy hardware play, the surge raises the question: What's changed?

The quick response: enterprise and hyperscale customers are upgrading their network gear sooner than planned, and many of those investments are directly associated with the build-out of AI data centers. The technology company's stock has climbed by approximately 45% since March 31 through the early part of July 2026; the bulk of the gains have been driven by a single earnings report in May.

Cisco's fiscal 3Q 2026 results, which wrap up on April 25, 2026, have come in well ahead of the consensus. The total revenue was $15.84 billion, up 12% year-over-year, and wider than the average analyst estimate of $15.56 billion, while adjusted EPS of $1.06 topped the forecast of $1.04, per CNBC.

The networking product segment, which is particularly affected by the AI-powered data center upgrades, registered a 25% revenue increase to $8.82 billion. Orders increased 35% YOY, and the forecasted revenue for the next quarter of $16.7-$16.9 billion was higher than analysts' estimates.
The company's stock jumped 15% after the report, and CNBC noted that the results would be Cisco's best since 2002.

Could You Catch The Next Run In Cisco Stock?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Cisco Systems (CSCO) stock returned 57.3% in the year to October 28, 2026, against 14.0% for the S&P 500. Over that year, management reported a jump in orders for its AI networking gear from the largest cloud companies. If that run could have been caught early, Cisco’s calls and filed results from before October 2025 should already show the business building. So what was Cisco saying back then?

During the fiscal Q1 2025 call on November 13, 2024, management said Cisco expected to beat its target of $1 billion in AI orders for that fiscal year. Because the company provided its own forecast on a public call almost a year before the period measured here, a reader could have acted on it.
Yet that $1 billion target was small next to the $56.7 billion in revenue Cisco reported for fiscal 2025. You could hear about AI orders early, but they still made up a small part of Cisco.

Total sales turned up, but full-year networking sales did not. Revenue fell 5.6% from a year earlier in the quarter ended October 2024, and was up 11.4% by the quarter ended April 2025, in results Cisco filed on May 20, 2025.
Management went further over the summer. During the fiscal Q4 2025 call on August 13, 2025, management reported record orders for AI infrastructure from its largest cloud customers.

Cisco’s full-year results for fiscal 2025, which ended in July 2025, did not yet show that shift. Networking sales fell 3.2% for the full year while security sales rose 59.5%, meaning Cisco’s return to growth that year came from outside networking. Management credited Splunk, a business Cisco was still integrating, with security orders that more than doubled.

Wells Fargo, Cisco, and 20 Other Companies Oppose Tokenization of Their Shares on OKXICE
sum: U.S. bank Wells Fargo, networking equipment manufacturer Cisco, and four other companies have opposed the trading of tokenized versions of their shares on the OKXICE platform. The total number of issuers who have filed objections has reached 22, according to an official document dated October 23.
The list now includes software developer Intuit, chip manufacturers Arm Holdings and Marvell Technology, as well as biotechnology company Moderna.
Previously, similar objections were filed by Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Verizon, Broadcom, Qualcomm, McDonald’s, and other corporations.

The number of objections has quickly increased—according to Decrypt, nine firms were listed on October 15, 16 on October 19, and 22 by October 23. The reasons for the objections are not specified in the document.

OKXICE is a joint project between cryptocurrency trading platform OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), which owns the New York Stock Exchange. The partners own the platform equally through subsidiaries.
According to the documentation, OKXICE will operate 24/7 and utilize Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on the XLayer network. Trading pairs will be formed with stablecoins, including USDC and USDG.
In the initial notice dated October 4, the parties planned to facilitate trading of 63 tokenized instruments representing shares of 62 issuers on the platform.

items.t: Wells Fargo, Cisco, Intuit Among 6 More Companies Objecting to Tokenized Stocks
sum: - Six more companies, including Wells Fargo, Cisco, and Marvell, have objected to trading of their shares on OKXICE TSV, according to its Oct. 23 notice.
- That brings the total to 22, up from nine on Oct. 15, though the notices don’t explain the companies’ reasons or what the objections do.
- The notice also discloses risks, including no circuit breakers beyond halts, no protections against transaction reordering, and smart contract upgrades without advance notice.
The list of companies that don’t want their shares traded on OKX and ICE’s planned tokenized stock venue keeps growing.

Wells Fargo, Cisco Systems, and Marvell Technology are among six new issuers named in an updated public notice from OKXICE TSV dated Friday. Arm Holdings, Moderna and Intuit round out the new additions. That brings the total to 22 objecting companies, up from 16 on Oct. 19 and nine on Oct. 15.

Earlier objectors include Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Verizon, Broadcom, and UnitedHealth Group. None of the notices explain the companies’ reasons, or what effect an objection has on whether a stock can trade on the platform.

Wells Fargo joins Goldman Sachs as the second major U.S. bank on the list. Arm, Cisco, and Marvell add more chip and networking heavyweights to a roster already crowded with tech names, including Microsoft, Broadcom and Qualcomm.

sum: On October 14, 2026: price 113.64 USD, trend sideways, RSI 53.3, support 106.43, resistance 118.39. technical analysis of csco stock. Momentum Gains — full…

Cisco shares fell 1.24% to $113.64 on Nasdaq, extending a five-day decline of 3.19% even as the stock remained higher over the past month. The pullback leaves the shares above their 20-day moving average, while MACD remains positive; together, those signals point to short-term pressure within a still broadly sideways trading pattern, rather than a clear break in trend.

Cisco’s last price is above its 20-day simple moving average (SMA) of $111.27, a level that tracks the average closing price over the past 20 trading days. But it is only slightly above the 50-day SMA of $112.13? No: at $113.64, the share price is above both averages, though the 50-day average itself is higher than the 20-day one. That ordering, alongside the absence of a recent moving-average crossover, offers no clear signal that the longer-term trend has turned decisively upward.

The 20-day average has a rising slope of 1.36% over five trading days, suggesting recent underlying support despite the latest declines. The stock sits about 60% of the way through its $106.43–$118.39 20-day range, closer to resistance than support. Over three months, shares have traded between $104.51 and $124.71, putting the current price inside a wider range rather than near either extreme.

As shown in the chart, the Bollinger Bands—bands that widen or narrow with price volatility—span $103.09 to $119.46, with the middle line at $111.27. Cisco’s 64% position within the bands places it above the midpoint but not near the upper edge. The 14.7% band width is described as normal, so the setup does not point to an unusually compressed market poised for a sharp move.

Momentum readings are mixed but not strongly bearish. The RSI is 53.3, a neutral reading: the Relative Strength Index measures the pace of recent gains and losses, and this level suggests neither stretched buying nor pronounced selling. The Stochastic reading is also neutral, with %K at 60.5 and %D at 69.9. Because %K is below %D, the indicator shows some near-term cooling, though not an extreme signal on its own.

Arista Stock Rises 64.7% YTD: Is There More Upside Ahead?
sum: Arista Networks, Inc.ANET has gained 64.7% year to date compared with the Internet software industry’s growth of 8.8%. The stock has outperformed the Zacks Computer & Technology sector and the S&P 500 during the same time frame.
It has underperformed its peers like Hewlett Packard Enterprise CompanyHPE but outperformed Cisco Systems, Inc.CSCO. HPE has gained 200.1%, and Cisco has increased 52.4% during this period.
AI Networking and Expanding Ethernet opportunity are Growth Drivers

Arista is benefiting from rapidly rising demand for Ethernet-based networking infrastructure used in AI data centers. The company said cumulative customers using its Etherlink AI-fabric switches had surpassed 100 by the second quarter of 2026 compared with only a handful of customers in 2024. Its newer 7060XE7 platform supports up to 1.6-terabit throughput. Features such as Smart System Upgrade (SSU) and Multipath Reliable Connection (MRC) are engineered to improve network reliability and accelerator utilization.

This creates an important opportunity as AI clusters become larger and more geographically distributed. Arista's Scale-Across architecture is designed to connect AI infrastructure across multiple locations. The company expects the Scale-Across switching and routing opportunity to reach roughly $15-$20 billion by 2030.

Enterprises’ transition toward high-speed switching has created a major opportunity for the company. Its portfolio, which consists of traditional Ethernet deployments to 1.6-terabit AI networking platforms, is witnessing sustained market-share gains.

Moreover, Arista’s growth opportunity is increasingly diversified beyond its traditional data-center switching. AI/cloud networking, campus and routing, and cognitive networking through software and services are high-margin areas where Arista is expanding its foothold.

sum: Three networking and optical stocks are surging well past the broader market today, but the gaps between their gains reveal something specific about where AI infrastructure demand is hitting a wall.

AI networking demand is lifting Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET | ANET Price Prediction), Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) and Ciena (NYSE:CIEN), with shares of the optical supplier pulling far ahead of the two switching vendors. No company announcement accounts for the gain in Arista stock, which sits inside a broader bid across networking and optical equipment. That leaves the relative size of the three moves as the clearest signal of where the market sees demand outrunning supply.

Are There Signs Cisco Stock Is Going To Swing Big?
sum: Cisco Systems (CSCO) grew product orders 35% year over year in fiscal Q4 2026. But management called its fiscal 2027 AI revenue forecast prudent. Strong orders, besides that caution, make the next twelve months harder to call for Cisco stock. So are there signs that Cisco stock will swing a lot over those twelve months?

Yes. The options market is pricing Cisco stock to move about as much as it just did. Implied volatility is the yearly movement in a stock that option buyers and sellers are paying for. Cisco’s one-year implied volatility is 36.7%. The same measure of the stock’s actual movement over the past year is 34.5%.
Those two readings are close, and the stock moved a lot over the past year. Its daily closing price ranged from $67.46 to $130.00 over that period.

The options market’s one-year range for Cisco stock has a floor of $75.03 and a ceiling of $154.39. Both are measured from a share price of $107.63 on September 30, 2026. The options behind that range expire on September 17, 2027.
In money, $10,000 of Cisco stock bought at that price would be worth $3,029 less at the floor. At the ceiling, it would be worth $4,345 more. Dividends are not counted in either figure.

The options market is pricing about two chances in three that the stock ends inside that range. That is a price for uncertainty, not a forecast. A finish below the floor is priced at a 21% chance, against 12% for a finish above the ceiling.

The open question for Cisco is how quickly its orders become revenue. Cisco took $9.3 billion of AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers in fiscal 2026. Management projected $7.5 billion of AI infrastructure revenue from its hyperscale business for fiscal 2027 and called that figure prudent. It also told investors on the fiscal Q4 2026 call to expect meaningfully higher orders.

sum: Cisco Systems stock (ISIN US17275R1023) is trading close to its 52-week high after the networking group reported record fiscal 2026 results, including fourth-quarter revenue growth of 18 percent to USD 17.3 billion as of September 9, 2026, according to Yahoo Finance.

As of fiscal year 2026, Cisco Systems delivered full-year revenue of USD 63.3 billion, up 12 percent from the previous fiscal year, underlining the company’s ability to grow while transitioning its architecture toward AI-centric networking, according to Yahoo Finance.

Fourth-quarter non-GAAP earnings per share reached USD 1.22, an increase of 23 percent year over year, while non-GAAP EPS for fiscal 2026 came in at USD 4.33, illustrating that profit growth outpaced revenue growth for the period, according to Yahoo Finance.

Cisco also reported USD 9.3 billion in AI infrastructure orders for fiscal 2026, roughly 4.5 times the prior-year level, highlighting how hyperscaler demand is becoming a central growth driver for the business, as noted by Yahoo Finance.

On the margin side, Cisco’s non-GAAP operating margin in fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 stood at 35.9 percent, up from 34.3 percent a year earlier, helped by the scale of hyperscaler AI orders that add revenue with limited incremental operating expense, according to Yahoo Finance.

At the same time, Cisco’s non-GAAP gross margin in fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 declined to 66.3 percent, down 210 basis points from 68.4 percent in the prior-year quarter, as higher hardware mix and elevated memory costs weighed on profitability, according to Tikr.

Despite these margin headwinds, management guided fiscal 2027 revenue above USD 72 billion, implying expected growth of roughly 13.8 percent versus the fiscal 2026 revenue base of USD 63.3 billion, which signals confidence in sustained demand for Cisco’s networking, security and AI infrastructure offerings, according to Yahoo Finance.

With an involvement in several other government defense projects, the company continues to reinforce its role in secure communications, tactical networking and mission-critical infrastructure while showcasing its ability to support large-scale, high-security deployments that meet evolving defense standards.

As governments increasingly prioritize border security and aerial threat mitigation, this collaboration could create new long-term growth opportunities for Nokia in rapidly growing security and enterprise markets.

The Smartest Dividend Stocks to Buy With $5,000 Right Now
sum: Dividend stocks give you the benefit of quarterly cash flow and long-term capital gains. However, not all dividend stocks are created equal. Not everyone wants to buy a stock like Micron that has impressive long-term gains but only a 0.06% yield. However, a high-yield dividend stock may present the opposite problem: high cash flow but low overall returns.

These three tech stocks are in the middle ground. They deliver solid fundamental growth while having respectable yields for new investors. Accumulating these three dividend stocks can prove to be a smart move in the long run.

IBM (IBM -0.85%) has a dividend yield above 2.5% and has almost doubled over the past five years. It has reinvented itself as an artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure provider that is investing heavily in quantum computing.

CEO Arvind Krishna cited AI as a "tailwind for our global business" in the first-quarter report. Overall revenue increased by 9% year over year, with the software and infrastructure segments both posting double-digit year-over-year growth rates.

President Donald Trump recently announced an executive order aimed at ramping up U.S. quantum computing investments and specifically mentioned IBM, saying he regretted selling the stock before entering office. It's a notable mention, since it confirms IBM remains on President Trump's radar as his administration continues to financially support specific companies amid the quantum computing expansion.

Quantum computing may turn into a major growth accelerator for the business. IBM said last year that it would invest $150 billion into this technology over the next five years, and it revealed an additional $10 billion investment into the industry that will be spread out over the next five years.
IBM is a mature business that gives investors exposure to exciting opportunities while offering a solid yield.

items.t: The Real Risk Inside Cisco Stock
sum: After a strong run, it’s natural for any Cisco Systems (CSCO) shareholder to feel confident. The stock is up 72% over the last year, powered by a story of transformation. The company is capturing surging AI demand, raising its forecast for AI infrastructure orders to $9 billion for the fiscal year. But when a stock has priced in this much success, the risks change. The question is no longer just about whether the company can grow, but whether it can grow in a way that justifies the new, higher expectations.
The very engine of this success, the pivot into AI hardware, may also be a significant vulnerability.

The increase in demand for Cisco’s AI-related hardware is clear, but it appears to be coming at a cost to profitability. In its most recent quarter, the company’s non-GAAP product gross margin was 64.3%, a figure that was down 330 basis points from the year before. Management pointed directly to the cause: “negative impacts from mix and higher memory costs.” This is the critical detail. As the business shifts more toward high-volume AI systems, it can pressure the company’s overall margin profile. If the new, fast-growing revenue is less profitable than the business it’s supplementing, then earnings may not grow as quickly as the top line. For a stock whose valuation depends on profit growth, that kind of margin compression, if it continues, could become a concern.

This brings us to the second risk: the valuation itself. The market has already given Cisco a lot of credit for its future. The stock currently trades at a price-to-sales multiple of 7.7, which is above its 10-year high of 5.2. To justify the premium, models suggest the company needs to deliver revenue growth of roughly 18.4% a year. That’s a high target. When expectations are this high, there is little room for error. A business stumble, a slight moderation in order growth, or a quarterly earnings miss can have a significant impact on the stock. The cushion for any disappointment has been removed by the recent rally, meaning even good news might not be good enough if it falls short of these expectations.
Ultimately, the market has rewarded Cisco for successfully capturing a new opportunity in AI.
